plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with correlated values. My value is $42. The common value is [0, 29] and taste adjustment is [0, 20]. A value of 42 is very high (maximum possible is 49), suggesting the common value is likely high, which means opponents likely have high values too. In a standard second-price auction with private values, bidding one's value is optimal. With correlated values, bidding slightly below value can be strategic, but since I want to maximize profit and 42 is strong, bidding my value is a robust strategy.

My value is $40. Since this is the only round, I want to win if my bid has a good chance of being profitable. Given the possible range of values (0-49), I'll bid slightly above what I estimate the second highest bid to be, aiming for a conservative win. I will bid $35.50, hoping to secure the win against other bidders who may have lower valuations.

Given my value of $29, and it being the final round, I want to win if possible, but avoid overpaying. Since values are redrawn each round, past history is irrelevant. I'll bid slightly above what I estimate the others might bid, aiming to secure the win without a large payment. A bid around $20 should be competitive, assuming others' values aren't drastically higher.
